This is the video for Module 1 of Negotiation Skills for Business and Life.
A negotiation is any conversation where people who need something from each other try to reach an agreement.
Buying fabric, a customer asking for a discount, rent with a landlord, pay with an employer.

say: The most useful idea in this course comes from the book Getting to Yes.
People usually argue over positions. A position is the specific thing someone says they want, like I will only pay 40000 naira. When you only argue positions, one person must lose.

panel.heading: Positions and interests
right: A fixed budget, a worry, a goal

say: Behind every position sits an interest. That is the need, worry or goal that answers the question why.
A supplier who demands full payment upfront may be worried about customers who never pay. When you understand interests, you can often find an option that satisfies both.

panel.heading: Positions and interests

say: Here are the four principles in plain words. One. Be soft on the person and firm on the issue.

panel.heading: The four principles
items: Separate the people from the problem
Focus on interests, not positions
Invent options for mutual gain
Insist on objective criteria

say: Two. Ask why, listen, and share your own interests too.

panel.heading: The four principles
items: Separate the people from the problem
Focus on interests, not positions
Invent options for mutual gain

say: Three. Before deciding, list several possible deals. Different payment timing, a bigger quantity, an added service.

items: Separate the people from the problem

say: Four. Use fair standards both sides can check, like current market prices or the cost of materials.

panel.heading: The four principles
items: Separate the people from the problem

say: Here is a worked example. Mrs Bello, a school administrator, wants 60 bags. Each bag costs Ngozi about 2800 naira to make.
Mrs Bello offers 3000 a bag. Ngozi's normal price is 4500. The gap is 90000 naira on the whole order. That is a fight of positions.
So Ngozi asks, can you tell me a bit about the budget and what the bags are for?
Now she learns the interest. The parents' association approved 200000 in total, and the bags must carry the school logo and be ready in three weeks.
Ngozi offers three options. Mrs Bello chooses 60 bags without the inner pocket at 3300 each, so 198000.
Ngozi keeps a profit of about 30000, and gets a repeat customer.
Many women lose money not because they cannot talk, but because they never decided their numbers in advance.
Your BATNA is your best alternative to a negotiated agreement. It is not a wish. It is a real option you could take tomorrow.

panel.heading: Write these down before you start
items: BATNA: what you will do if this deal fails
Walk-away point: the worst deal you accept
Target: a good result you can justify
ZOPA: where both walk-away points overlap

say: Your walk-away point comes from your BATNA. Never accept a deal worse than your best alternative.

say: Your target is the good, realistic result you are aiming for.

say: And the ZOPA, the zone of possible agreement, is the range between the seller's walk-away point and the buyer's. A deal can only happen inside it.

say: Halima's neighbour will still buy the freezer this month.
So her BATNA is 120000 naira, and that is her walk-away point.
She checks similar freezers online and with two repairers, then sets her target at 155000.
Chinedu privately will pay up to 145000. So the ZOPA is 120000 to 145000.
Halima opens at 160000. Chinedu offers 125000. They settle at 140000.
Halima earned 20000 more than her BATNA, because she knew her numbers and did not panic at a low first offer. Keep your walk-away point private.
Some negotiations carry risk beyond money. Meet strangers in public or familiar places, and take someone with you if you can.
Never pay a deposit to someone you have not verified. Check payment alerts in your bank app, not a screenshot. Never share your BVN, card PIN or one-time codes.
And saying, let me think about it and get back to you tomorrow, is always acceptable.

panel.heading: Protect yourself first
items: Meet strangers in public places
No deposit to anyone you have not verified
Check payment alerts in your bank app
Never share your BVN, PIN or codes
You are allowed to pause

say: To remember. A position is what someone asks for, an interest is why. Be soft on the person and firm on the problem.
Never accept a deal worse than your BATNA, and keep your walk-away point private. And verify people and payments before money changes hands.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Position is what, interest is why
Be soft on the person, firm on the problem
Never accept less than your BATNA
Keep your walk-away point to yourself
Verify people and payments first
